subtopic: Scalars and Vectors
stem: State, for each of the following physical quantities, if it is a scalar or a vector : volume, mass, speed, acceleration, density, number of moles, velocity, angular frequency, displacement, angular velocity.

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Establish the following vector inequality geometrically or otherwise :

(a) \(|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| \le |\mathbf{a}| + |\mathbf{b}|\)

When does the equality sign above apply?

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Establish the following vector inequality geometrically or otherwise :

(b) \(|\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| \ge \big|\,|\mathbf{a}| - |\mathbf{b}|\,\big|\)

When does the equality sign above apply?

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Given \(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{d} = 0\), state whether the following statement is correct :

(a) \(\mathbf{a}\), \(\mathbf{b}\), \(\mathbf{c}\), and \(\mathbf{d}\) must each be a null vector.

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Given \(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{d} = 0\), state whether the following statement is correct :

(b) The magnitude of \((\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{c})\) equals the magnitude of \((\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{d})\).

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Given \(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{d} = 0\), state whether the following statement is correct :

(c) The magnitude of \(\mathbf{a}\) can never be greater than the sum of the magnitudes of \(\mathbf{b}\), \(\mathbf{c}\), and \(\mathbf{d}\).

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem:
Given \(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{d} = 0\), state whether the following statement is correct :

(d) \(\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c}\) must lie in the plane of \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{d}\) if \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{d}\) are not collinear, and in the line of \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{d}\), if they are collinear?

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem: Three girls skating on a circular ice ground of radius \(200\,\text{m}\) start from a point \(P\) on the edge of the ground and reach a point \(Q\) diametrically opposite to \(P\) following different paths as shown in Fig. 3.19. What is the magnitude of the displacement vector for each ? For which girl is this equal to the actual length of path skate ?

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem: A cyclist starts from the centre \(O\) of a circular park of radius \(1\,\text{km}\), reaches the edge \(P\) of the park, then cycles along the circumference, and returns to the centre along \(QO\) as shown in Fig. 3.20. If the round trip takes \(10\,\text{min}\), what is the (a) net displacement, (b) average velocity, and (c) average speed of the cyclist ?

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem: On an open ground, a motorist follows a track that turns to his left by an angle of \(60^{\circ}\) after every \(500\,\text{m}\). Starting from a given turn, specify the displacement of the motorist at the third, sixth and eighth turn. Compare the magnitude of the displacement with the total path length covered by the motorist in each case.

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem: A passenger arriving in a new town wishes to go from the station to a hotel located \(10\,\text{km}\) away on a straight road from the station. A dishonest cabman takes him along a circuitous path \(23\,\text{km}\) long and reaches the hotel in \(28\,\text{min}\). What is (a) the average speed of the taxi, (b) the magnitude of average velocity ? Are the two equal ?

subtopic: Projectile Motion
stem: The ceiling of a long hall is \(25\,\text{m}\) high. What is the maximum horizontal distance that a ball thrown with a speed of \(40\,\text{m s}^{-1}\) can go without hitting the ceiling of the hall ?

subtopic: Projectile Motion
stem: A cricketer can throw a ball to a maximum horizontal distance of \(100\,\text{m}\). How much high above the ground can the cricketer throw the same ball ?

subtopic: Uniform Circular Motion
stem: A stone tied to the end of a string \(80\,\text{cm}\) long is whirled in a horizontal circle with a constant speed. If the stone makes \(14\) revolutions in \(25\,\text{s}\), what is the magnitude and direction of acceleration of the stone ?

subtopic: Uniform Circular Motion
stem: An aircraft executes a horizontal loop of radius \(1.00\,\text{km}\) with a steady speed of \(900\,\text{km/h}\). Compare its centripetal acceleration with the acceleration due to gravity.

subtopic: Uniform Circular Motion
stem:
Read the statement below carefully and state, with reasons, if it is true or false :

(a) The net acceleration of a particle in circular motion is **always** along the radius of the circle towards the centre.

subtopic: Uniform Circular Motion
stem:
Read the statement below carefully and state, with reasons, if it is true or false :

(b) The velocity vector of a particle at a point is **always** along the tangent to the path of the particle at that point.

subtopic: Uniform Circular Motion
stem:
Read the statement below carefully and state, with reasons, if it is true or false :

(c) The acceleration vector of a particle in **uniform** circular motion averaged over one cycle is a null vector.

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
The position of a particle is given by

\(\mathbf{r} = 3.0t\,\hat{\mathbf{i}} - 2.0t^{2}\,\hat{\mathbf{j}} + 4.0\,\hat{\mathbf{k}}\,\text{m}\)

where \(t\) is in seconds and the coefficients have the proper units for \(\mathbf{r}\) to be in metres.

(a) Find the \(\mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{a}\) of the particle? (b) What is the magnitude and direction of velocity of the particle at \(t = 2.0\,\text{s}\) ?

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem: A particle starts from the origin at \(t = 0\,\text{s}\) with a velocity of \(10.0\,\hat{\mathbf{j}}\,\text{m/s}\) and moves in the \(x\)-\(y\) plane with a constant acceleration of \(\left(8.0\,\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 2.0\,\hat{\mathbf{j}}\right)\,\text{m s}^{-2}\). (a) At what time is the \(x\)-coordinate of the particle \(16\,\text{m}\)? What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the particle at that time? (b) What is the speed of the particle at the time ?

subtopic: Addition, Subtraction and Resolution of Vectors
stem: \(\hat{\mathbf{i}}\) and \(\hat{\mathbf{j}}\) are unit vectors along \(x\)- and \(y\)-axis respectively. What is the magnitude and direction of the vectors \(\hat{\mathbf{i}} + \hat{\mathbf{j}}\), and \(\hat{\mathbf{i}} - \hat{\mathbf{j}}\) ? What are the components of a vector \(\mathbf{A} = 2\,\hat{\mathbf{i}} + 3\,\hat{\mathbf{j}}\) along the directions of \(\hat{\mathbf{i}} + \hat{\mathbf{j}}\) and \(\hat{\mathbf{i}} - \hat{\mathbf{j}}\)? [You may use graphical method]

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
For any arbitrary motion in space, state whether the following relation is true :

(a) \(\mathbf{v}_{\text{average}} = (1/2)\left(\mathbf{v}(t_1) + \mathbf{v}(t_2)\right)\)

(The 'average' stands for average of the quantity over the time interval \(t_1\) to \(t_2\).)

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
For any arbitrary motion in space, state whether the following relation is true :

(b) \(\mathbf{v}_{\text{average}} = \dfrac{\mathbf{r}(t_2) - \mathbf{r}(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}\)

(The 'average' stands for average of the quantity over the time interval \(t_1\) to \(t_2\).)

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
For any arbitrary motion in space, state whether the following relation is true :

(c) \(\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{v}(0) + \mathbf{a}\,t\)

(The 'average' stands for average of the quantity over the time interval \(t_1\) to \(t_2\).)

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
For any arbitrary motion in space, state whether the following relation is true :

(d) \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{r}(0) + \mathbf{v}(0)\,t + (1/2)\,\mathbf{a}\,t^{2}\)

(The 'average' stands for average of the quantity over the time interval \(t_1\) to \(t_2\).)

subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration
stem:
For any arbitrary motion in space, state whether the following relation is true :

(e) \(\mathbf{a}_{\text{average}} = \dfrac{\mathbf{v}(t_2) - \mathbf{v}(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}\)

(The 'average' stands for average of the quantity over the time interval \(t_1\) to \(t_2\).)
